key_evidence: (a) The offline metric compares the baseline with its own samples. In policy_rollout51.py:1492 and 1507-1510, a label is the executed stream from an observation. For every H10 branch sample, every H50 sample at rel%50==0, and every H10 student sample (obs_every=10 and trajectory_every=10 line up with the replan points), label[:10] IS the baseline's own chunk[:10] from the same rendered observation, drawn with different noise. That covers 886 of 1310 dataset labels (67.6%) and 137 of the 160 recovery examples offline_fit sampled.

The rise in offline error follows alignment, not horizon or origin. Paired step200 minus baseline, first-10 RMS: H10 aligned n=44 +0.0053 (se 0.0027, 37/44 up); H50 aligned n=13 +0.0076 (se 0.0040, 12/13 up); H50 non-aligned n=23 +0.00007 (se 0.0025, 14/23 up); student (all aligned) n=80 +0.0094 (se 0.0024, 63/80 up). Steps 100 and 300 give the same pattern. Labels that are not a same-observation self-sample did not move at all.

Retention demos (labels not generated by the policy): +0.0010, +0.0028 and +0.0022 at steps 100/200/300, se about 0.002, t 0.5-1.1, 38-44 of 64 up. The 64 frames come from only 4 episodes, and per-episode diffs are +0.012, -0.007, +0.004, +0.002. Also, finetune.json says the baseline's raster adaptation used 91 episodes / 18200 frames, which matches storm_capture100's 91 files x 200 frames. So the retention episodes (ep833/864/176/354) were very likely in the baseline's own training data (inferred from counts), and even this guard measures movement off a fitted minimum.

The pattern by error quartile is what perturbing a self-sampled metric looks like, not drift away from targets. Branch: Q1 (baseline error <0.015) ratio 1.66, Q4 ratio 0.97 (diff -0.008). Retention: Q1 1.30, Q4 0.98. The size is ~0.005 rad RMS over 10 actions, about 10x smaller than label spread (median 0.055) and closed-loop replan jumps (0.24-0.27 rad).

The regime demonstrably learns. The anchor-fit metric (first 8 frames of 4 held-out storm_capture100 episodes, the same distribution as the anchor) fell from 0.1333 to 0.0852/0.0761/0.0812 at steps 100/200/300 for a1. v2 iter1 gave 0.0867/0.0753/0.0823, iter2 0.0861/0.0766/0.0830, iter3 0.0869/0.0755/0.0813. That is -35% to -43%, the four runs agree within about 1.5%, and it generalises to held-out episodes. Meanwhile whole-episode retention loss rose +6/+9/+10% and breached at step 300 (0.07874 vs limit 0.07861). This is a directed trade of whole-episode fit for episode-start fit, not noise pulling away from all targets.

The four fine-tunes are not independent tests of 'different data'. Replaying the trainer's sampler reproduces v2's recorded mean_sampled_awr_weight exactly (2.24977939/2.31676696/2.2152263 for iter1; 13.59996611/14.66688732/13.1362698 for iter3). The replay shows the anchor index sequence (rollout_weighted_finetune.py:397, seed 4242) is identical across iter1-3 and a1, over the same 128 anchor frames. Per-sample exposure: anchor 600 draws / 128 = 4.7 visits per frame; recovery 600 / 1310 = 0.46, and 63.7% of recovery labels were never drawn.

No random walk. Per-example changes at steps 100/200/300 correlate 0.78-0.92. On aligned branch examples, RMS |c300-c100| = 0.0067 vs |c100-b| = 0.0159, where a random walk predicts about 1.4x (~0.022). Successive increments are anti-correlated (-0.68 branch aligned, -0.41 retention). The model moved to a new point within 100 steps and then fluctuated around it.

Recovery labels the trainer actually drew did not move toward those labels. Branch at step 300: drawn n=23 +0.0077 (se 0.0014) vs never drawn n=57 +0.0025 (se 0.0021). Student at step 300: drawn +0.0056 (se 0.0019) vs never drawn +0.0096 (se 0.0041). At 0.46 visits per label, no per-label learning is detectable. This fits the working diagnosis as much as exposure or dilution, so it cannot tell them apart.

(c) boundary unfreeze is refuted. The original BC run (train_config.json: train_expert_only=True, freeze_vision_encoder=True) trained the same action-expert plus projection subspace (155 tensors, 99.9M parameters). The labels are the baseline's own outputs, so they are expressible by construction, and this subspace moved anchor-fit by 40%.

(d) closed loop. a1 dev05 finished at 15:51Z as a settled 4/4, so the screen is 1/8, mean conditions 2.375, not 0/8. Paired against the same-campaign v3 baseline, the four fine-tunes differ by -0.375, 0.000 (iter2 identical on all 8 poses), -0.125 and -0.125 conditions. Against the v2 baseline they differ by -0.875 to -0.5. The baseline against itself on identical seeds differed by -0.5 (per-pose sd 0.93; se of an 8-pose mean about 0.33). Settled success is 2/32 for fine-tunes vs 2/16 for baseline (Fisher p=0.59). A pooled within-pose permutation test gives one-sided p=0.035 on conditions, driven mostly by the high v2 baseline run. At H50 there is no drop: 4/8, 3/8, 4/8 (mean 3.25/3.125/3.25) vs 4/8 (3.125).

The supervision carries little information the baseline lacks. All 1310 labels are baseline-executed actions. 27 of 32 settled successes, and 1085/1310 labels (83%), come from the 3 rows where the baseline's own student episode already succeeded. 372 labels (28%) come from Seen_5_key1 roots 150/250/350, which were already at 4/4 at the root (12/12 branches succeed; nothing to select). On rows where the student failed, branches succeeded 5/80 (6%), leaving 225 labels (17%). Branch success was 16/64 at both H10 and H50.

A consistent side-signal: the labels are stitched executed streams. Mean per-step L2 at replan junctions inside labels is 0.222 rad, vs 0.105 for interior steps and 0.069-0.093 for demo chunks. In closed loop, the mean replan-boundary jump at H10 is 0.270-0.274 in all four fine-tunes vs 0.235/0.241 in the two baseline runs, and rises on 6-7 of 8 poses for each fine-tune. Plausible contributor; not tested causally.
alternative_explanations: Best supported for the offline-fit result, (a) metric artifact: offline_fit.py compares one fixed-seed draw against labels that for 68% of the dataset (86% of the sampled examples) are the baseline's own draw from the same observation. Any change to the model raises it, and labels that are not self-samples show zero change. A candidate could also pass by collapsing its own sampling variance without learning anything.

Best supported for what the fine-tunes actually learned, (b) anchor dominance: an identical 128-frame episode-start anchor stream in all four runs, at ~10x the per-sample exposure of the rollout data, cut held-out episode-start loss by ~40% every time while whole-episode retention loss rose 6-10%. It shows a real learned direction, but a closed-loop causal link to the anchor is not shown: first-100-step end-effector-to-cloth distance is inconsistent across fine-tunes.

Best supported for 'no improvement', low information in the supervision: every label is baseline behaviour, 83% from rows the baseline already solves, 28% from roots already folded 4/4, and only 17% from rows the baseline fails. Even a perfect fit approximates the baseline. The 4/8 screen needs roughly a 4x jump over a ~12% baseline.

(d) Closed-loop drop is small and marginal, not established. vs the same-campaign baseline it is -0.16 conditions on average (range 0 to -0.375); settled success is 2/32 vs 2/16; H50 is unchanged. The baseline differed from itself by 0.5 on identical seeds.

Stitched-label artifact: 50-step targets contain replan-junction jumps about 2-3x larger than demos, and all four fine-tunes show about 13% larger replan-boundary jumps at H10. Plausible H10-specific mechanism, untested.
(c) boundary-only unfreeze: refuted. It is the same parameter subspace that produced the baseline, and it moved anchor-fit by 40%.

Partial support for the working diagnosis: drawn recovery labels did not move toward their targets. At 0.46 visits per label this is equally explained by under-exposure and dilution, so it does not single out gradient noise.

refute.recommendation:
Do not run attempt 2 as currently written. 'Noise-dominated optimisation' is not the best-supported explanation. The offline increase is a self-sample artifact: it is zero on non-self labels. The one signal the regime clearly learned was the shared 128-frame anchor: held-out episode-start loss fell ~40% in all four runs. The closed-loop 'degradation' is marginal: -0.16 conditions against the same-campaign baseline, success 2/32 vs 2/16, no drop at H50. The deeper cause of 'no improvement' is supervision that is ~83% the baseline's own behaviour on rows it already solves.

Two points block the plan as drafted.
1. The offline gate as drafted cannot be passed by any candidate that has actually changed, except through variance collapse. If a gate is kept, pre-register it on:
   - non-self labels (H50 non-aligned, plus the recovery samples from roots held out of training);
   - K>=8 noise seeds per example, with paired CIs against the baseline's own seed-to-seed spread;
   - or the flow-matching loss with fixed noise and time, plus a chunk-consistency check (overlap between chunks predicted 10 steps apart).
2. Batch 32 via 8x4 accumulation at 300 steps is not a one-factor change. It also raises exposure: recovery to ~3.7 visits per label, anchor to ~37 visits per frame. That amplifies the anchor mechanism the evidence implicates. If it is run anyway, pre-register anchor_fit and retention as the readout: a further anchor_fit drop together with a retention breach supports anchor dominance, not noise.

The evidence points to two better single factors:
- the anchor (reduce its fraction, or draw it from whole episodes rather than first-8 frames);
- label informativeness (restrict to the 225 labels from roots the student fails, and drop labels from roots already at 4/4).

Also use a different seed from v2/v3, or several seeds: all four prior fine-tunes shared the byte-identical anchor stream, so they are not independent replicates. Mind the screen's power: P(>=4/8) is 0.11 at a true rate of 0.25 and 0.41 at 0.40. Given the remaining budget (37 tasks, 16 reserved for the final set), a cheaper step first is to check offline, on the existing a1 checkpoints, whether non-self-label error, retention error and replan consistency separate the candidates from baseline, before spending the 8-task screen.

key_evidence: DTYPE (decisive): the trainable action expert is stored and updated in bf16. In baseline/original-BC safetensors, lm_expert is BF16 for 96,607,440 params and F32 for 1,638,400; vision is F32 (86.4M). Rebuilding an expert the way lerobot does it (smolvlm_with_expert.py:95,105 AutoModel.from_config on a deepcopy of text_config, whose dtype is bfloat16, transformers 4.57.6) gives {torch.bfloat16}. The a1 checkpoints are byte-size-identical and keep BF16, so training ran on bf16 weights. rollout_weighted_finetune.py:287 builds AdamW directly on them, and a CPU check shows AdamW's exp_avg and exp_avg_sq are bf16 too.

Measured weight diff, baseline vs a1 step 100/200/300: 11.58%/11.56%/11.54% of the lm_expert bf16 weights changed. By |w| bin at step 300: <1e-3 99.5%, 1e-3..2.5e-3 96.8%, 2.5e-3..5e-3 50.7%, 5e-3..1e-2 0.0004%, >=1e-2 0.0000%. All 23,760 bf16 RMSNorm gains are unchanged. fp32 lm_expert cross-attn k/v and the fp32 projections (1.64M + 1.64M) changed 99.999%, relative norm 5.8e-3 to 6.9e-3. The cutoff is where half-ULP (about |w|/256) exceeds an Adam step of about lr = 1e-5, i.e. |w| > about 2.6e-3 to 3.9e-3. Of the 99,880,992 params recorded as trainable, only about 3.3M fp32 plus an 11% sliver of the smallest-magnitude bf16 weights can move, and that sliver moves in quantised +/-1-ULP jumps.

Raster fine-tune that built the baseline (bc_smolvla_seed0/030000 -> raster_ft_full, vision+action, lr 1e-5, 3000 steps): the same 11.4974% of lm_expert bf16 weights changed, but the fp32 vision tower changed 99.9999% (relative norm 1.73e-2). Its adaptation went through fp32 parameters. v3/v2 'boundary' mode excludes vision, so most of its payload is the frozen-by-rounding bf16 expert. This, not batch size, is the mechanical difference between the trainer that worked and the four that did not.

CPU simulation (200k weights ~N(0,0.02), 300 AdamW steps, lr 1e-5, wd 0.01): the bf16 update keeps cos 0.37 / 0.36 / 0.28 with the intended fp32 update at gradient SNR 10 / 1 / 0.1, and 84-85% of coordinates never move. Even a noise-free gradient cannot get past bf16 rounding, so a larger batch alone cannot fix the expert.

Offline fit, paired by example with common seeds (analysis/offline-fit-a1.json): at step 200, branch is +5.4% (+0.0042 rad, 95% CI [+0.0004,+0.0075], 79% of examples worse) and student is +11.8% (CI [+0.0052,+0.0142]). Retention demos are +2.4% with a CI spanning 0. The damage is fully present at step 100 (+5.4% / +9.5%) and does not grow after that. The model got measurably worse on its own training labels.

Not 'drift away from ALL targets': the anchor-distribution metric (first 8 frames of 4 held-out demos) falls 0.1333 -> 0.085/0.076/0.081 in a1. It followed almost the same path in v2 it1 (0.087/0.075/0.082), it2 (0.086/0.077/0.083) and it3 (0.087/0.0755/0.081), even though the supervision differed each time. Learning direction is set by what the four fine-tunes share (anchor half-batch, bf16-limited parameter set, optimizer), not by the supervision.

Anchor content (manifest training.anchor frames=8; rollout_weighted_finetune.py:157-159 x[:frames_per_file]): storm_capture ep2 frames 0-7 show state snapping from the reset pose [-1.136,0,0,0,0,0,1.136,0,...] to the ready pose, with |a0-state| 1.00/0.84/0.69/0.38/0.06 rad. Mean |a0-state| is 0.48-0.92 rad on joints 0-3 and 6-9 for the anchor versus 0.02-0.14 for recovery labels. Normalised reset-pose state reaches about +/-3.5 sigma on joints 0 and 6. At batch 4 with fraction 0.5, a1 made 600 anchor draws over 128 frames (about 4.7 passes) versus 600 recovery draws over 1310 (0.46 passes, about 37% coverage).

Checked and NOT defects. (a) Two-forward aggregation at :398-399 is a count-weighted mean of per-forward means, equal to the mean over the combined batch. There is no batch norm, and language padding is 'longest' with one task string. (b) Train/eval: text attention_dropout is 0.0, and SmolVLMWithExpertModel.train() forces the VLM to eval because train_expert_only=true, so train and eval forwards are identical. (c) AdamW default wd 0.01 shrinks weights by lr*wd = 1e-7 per step (3e-5 over 300 steps), below bf16 resolution and negligible in fp32. The raster trainer used the same default. (d) Trainer batch() :290-298 matches runner make_observation (policy_rollout51.py:762-774): uint8 HWC to float/255 CHW, same camera order, same pre pipeline (newline + tokenizer + MEAN_STD for state/action), same stats file. Units are radians in the normaliser stats, anchor and recovery labels alike. (e) Recovery awr_weight is uniformly 1.0 and labels are full 50-step chunks, so no actions_id_pad is needed. (f) The RNG save/restore around held-out evaluation (:317-336) is correct. (g) grad clip 1.0 (vs 10.0 in the original run) and no warmup are deviations, but Adam largely normalises gradient scale away.

Cost and memory: the a1 train job took 312 s total for 300 steps plus loading, 6 evaluations and 3 saves (0.087 GPU-h), i.e. about 1 min per 100 steps. In boundary mode the vision/VLM are frozen and only the state token's path through the VLM needs activations for backward, so per-sample memory is below the raster fine-tune's vision+action batch 8, which ran on the same GPU class.
alternative_explanations: Pure gradient noise: a 2+2-sample flow-matching step plus Adam's sign-like early updates (no warmup) could push a converged model uphill on everything. It is partly consistent with the plateau by step 100. It does not explain the anchor metric falling 43% the same way in all four runs, or why a noise-free gradient still could not move 88% of the expert (simulation).

The anchor pulls the model away: half of every batch is the home-to-ready snap, which has large, easily fit targets and far-out-of-distribution states. The only freely movable parameters are global linear maps (state_proj, action_in/out_proj, action_time_mlp, cross-attn k/v), so fitting the snap moves outputs at every state. This fits the anchor metric falling while recovery-label RMS rises and retention loss rises about 10%. It is confounded with the bf16 restriction, and the existing data cannot separate the two.

Supervision reach: 0.46 passes (about 37% of recovery samples ever drawn) is too little to learn 1310 labels, independent of noise. This explains the absence of improvement but not the significant worsening on the labels themselves.

Label/transfer problems (label quality, garment-difficulty confounds, sim nondeterminism) would explain a flat closed-loop screen. They cannot explain an offline fit getting worse on the very labels the model was trained on, so they are secondary for the trainer question.

The offline-fit gate as implemented samples its 80+80 examples from the training set itself. At 3.66 passes about 97% will have been trained on, so the gate tests fitting, not generalisation, to new states. A root-held-out split would be needed to test generalisation.

trainer.recommendation: Attempt 2 should be a repair plus one factor, and the repair comes first because it is a correctness fix, not a tuning knob. (1) In rollout_weighted_finetune.py, after parameter_selection and before building the optimiser, cast the trainable parameters to fp32 (e.g. policy.model.vlm_with_expert.lm_expert.float(); the forward already casts hidden states per layer at smolvlm_with_expert.py:223,308,349-359,470). Adam state and .grad accumulation then run in fp32. Checkpoints get re-rounded to bf16 at evaluation load, because from_pretrained rebuilds the expert in bf16, but 300 steps of accumulated delta survive one final rounding where 300 separate rounding steps did not. offline_fit.py loads through the same path, so the gate measures the deployed weights. Also record wd/betas/clip/dtype and per-source losses. (2) The single preregistered optimisation factor: effective batch 32 by gradient accumulation of 8 micro-steps x 4 samples (2 recovery + 2 anchor each, exactly a1's proven step, so activation memory is unchanged; the extra fp32 weights, grads and Adam state for 96.6M params add about 1.5 GB, trivial on 48 GB). A 4 x 8 micro-batch is also safe, since the raster fine-tune ran batch 8 with the heavier vision+action unfreeze. Keep lr 1e-5 (the raster-FT value), steps 300 (the trainer cap), rollout_fraction 0.5, boundary unfreeze, same data and seed. That gives 16 recovery samples per step x 300 = 4,800 draws, about 3.66 passes over 1,310 (about 97% of samples seen at least once, vs 0.46 passes and about 37% in a1). Wall time is about 8x a1's stepping, roughly 20-30 min, one GPU task. Warn in the plan that anchor exposure rises to 37.5 passes over 128 home-to-ready frames. If the offline gate fails with the anchor metric collapsing again, the anchor composition, not batch, is the next single factor. Do NOT run batch-32 without the dtype repair: my prediction is that it fails the same way, because 88% of the expert still cannot move and bf16 .grad accumulation is lossy. (3) Before the 8-task screen, spend 1 train + 1 offline-fit task on a paired gate. The candidate's mean first-10 RMS must be below baseline on both branch and student labels, with a paired bootstrap 95% CI excluding zero, using a1's harness and seeds; a1 itself fails this at step 200 (+5.4% [+0.0004,+0.0075], +11.8% [+0.0052,+0.0142]). Also report retention RMS, and check the weight diff (share of expert weights changed should be well above 11.5%) to confirm the repair took effect. Evaluating on recovery roots held out from training would make the gate test generalisation rather than fitting.

The replan at rel%horizon==0 (1491-1492) uses that same image and joint. a = plan[rel % horizon] (1493). The settle repeats actions[-1] (1498), matching the student's settle on its last action. Label content: 68% of labels (596 H10-branch + 122 H50 at rel%50==0 + 168 student) have first-10 rows that are a fresh baseline sample drawn at that exact observation. Only 424 (32%, H50 at rel%50 in 10..40) are off-distribution, older open-loop plan rows. Two independent-seed labels at the same observation differ by mean first-10 RMS 0.058 (n=29), the same scale as the offline-fit baseline error (0.0775 branch / 0.0799 student). The baseline is sitting at its own sampling-noise floor.

Weak selection: 372 branch examples come from roots where 4/4 candidates settled (no filtering) and 339 from 3/4 roots. 1085/1310 (83%) come from the 3 rows where the student had already settled on its own.

Offline-fit deltas vs baseline (paired, same seed per example), split by label type: fresh labels worsen by +0.0069/+0.0079/+0.0070 at steps 100/200/300 (±0.0016, n=137, about 80% of examples worse). Stale labels are flat: -0.0002/+0.0001/-0.0005 (±0.002-0.0026, n=23), where pure drift would predict +0.006 to +0.008. Fresh-vs-stale difference z = 2.5-3.1 (one result; the three checkpoints are correlated). Retention deltas are +0.001/+0.003/+0.002 (±0.002).

Splitting by root success rate is inconclusive: the low-success (1-2/4) subgroup has only n=29 (5 stale), with overlapping error bars. Aggregate rms_chunk50 rises at step 200 (branch 0.160 -> 0.195, retention 0.208 -> 0.240), consistent with the retention-guard breach.
alternative_explanations: The labels carry little new information, so there is nothing for the fine-tune to converge toward. Most labels are the baseline's own samples at the same observation, and many come from roots where every candidate succeeded or from episodes the student already solved. On those rows the flow-matching gradient has roughly zero expected value, so training adds only drift at any batch size. That matches the regression being confined to fresh labels.

synthesis.diagnosis_summary: The "noise-dominated optimisation" diagnosis does not hold as stated. Three convergent findings replace it. (1) The offline-fit rise is largely a self-sample metric artifact: 67.6% of dataset labels (86% of sampled examples) are the baseline's own chunk drawn at the identical observation, so the baseline sits at its own sampling-noise floor (~0.058 RMS); paired deltas show the regression confined to self-sample-aligned labels (+0.005-0.009 rad) while non-self H50 labels moved +0.00007 (nothing), and per-example changes at steps 100/200/300 correlate 0.78-0.92 with anti-correlated increments — a move to a nearby point within 100 steps, not a random walk away from all targets. (2) The regime demonstrably learned a directed signal: held-out anchor-fit fell ~40% (0.133 to 0.076-0.085) nearly identically in all four fine-tunes regardless of supervision, implicating the shared 128-frame home-to-ready anchor (byte-identical stream, seed 4242, ~10x the per-sample exposure of recovery data), not gradient noise. (3) A real trainer defect: the lm_expert loads in bf16 and AdamW (with bf16 exp_avg/exp_avg_sq, no fp32 master copy) runs directly on it, so at lr 1e-5 every update below half-ULP rounds away — 88.5% of the 96.6M expert weights and all RMSNorm gains never moved in 300 steps; a1 effectively trained ~3.3M fp32 params, not the recorded 99.88M. Secondary but real: the supervision carries little information (all 1310 labels are baseline-executed actions; 83% from rows the student already solved; 28% from roots already at 4/4), and closed-loop "degradation" is marginal (-0.16 conditions vs same-campaign baseline; a1 screen was 1/8, mean 2.375, not 0/8; H50 unchanged at 3.125-3.25 vs 3.125; baseline differs from itself by 0.5 on identical seeds). Label alignment and dataset integrity are fully verified clean — do not blame the data pipeline. Larger batch alone cannot fix any of this: a noise-free gradient still cannot cross bf16 rounding (CPU simulation: 84-85% of coordinates never move even at SNR 10).

risks: Clock: the driver hardcodes irreversible campaign finalization at 17:51:44Z (driver.py:580-586); the required refreeze cannot finish in the ~70 remaining minutes, so if the user does not cancel/hold ticks 21401952 and 21401704 before then, attempt 2 is lost regardless of this plan. The check runs at tick time, so no tick may execute after the deadline until the plan is committed.

Refreeze fragility: verify_sources exits 5 on any drift and two training failures permanently end attempt 2; committing plans/attempt2.json before the refreeze and smoke are complete is the single most likely way to lose the attempt. The plan commit must be last.

Attribution confound: repair (fp32) and factor (batch 32) change together; if attempt 2 succeeds we cannot say which mattered, and if it fails we cannot exonerate either. Accepted deliberately; partial attribution via weight-diff, anchor_fit trajectory and per-source losses.

Anchor amplification (most likely scientific failure mode): anchor exposure rises to ~37.5 passes over 128 home-to-ready frames — the one direction all four prior fine-tunes demonstrably learned. With the expert genuinely movable, the retention guard may breach at BOTH step 200 and 300, ending attempt 2 with no candidate (cost 2 tasks). Preregistered as informative: that outcome plus a repeated anchor_fit collapse confirms anchor dominance and makes anchor composition the next campaign's factor.

Low supervision information: all 1310 labels are baseline-executed actions, 83% from rows the student already solved, 28% from roots already at 4/4, only 225 labels (17%) from rows the baseline fails — even a perfect fit approximates the baseline, so a null closed-loop result would not distinguish optimizer failure from label poverty.

Screen power: P(>= 4/8) is ~0.11 at a true per-pose rate of 0.25 and ~0.41 at 0.40; H10 outcomes carry ±0.5 mean-conditions noise on identical seeds (GPU cloth physics is not deterministic), so a genuinely improved candidate can fail the unchanged >= 4/8 threshold.

bf16 re-rounding at load: from_pretrained rebuilds the expert in bf16, so the deployed candidate carries one final rounding of the fp32 delta; sub-half-ULP components are discarded and the closed-loop effect may be smaller than the training-time fit suggests. The weight-diff gate is computed on reloaded weights for exactly this reason. Checkpoint size also grows (~200 MB fp32 expert tensors) unless save-side handling is added.

Gate residual weakness: even redefined, the offline-fit RMS comparison is in-sample and necessary-only; a candidate could pass (a)+(b) by moving weights without learning anything useful, or pass (b) partly via variance collapse. It is never reported as evidence of improvement.

Stale-label pull: 424 H50 labels are older open-loop plan continuations with 2-3x larger replan-junction jumps than demos; all four prior fine-tunes showed ~13% larger H10 replan-boundary jumps. Better fitting of these labels at batch 32 could actively hurt H10 replanning; the per-class RMS split is the preregistered readout, but the mechanism is untested causally.

New-code risk: the accumulation loop, fp32 cast, driver fit stage and multi-seed offline_fit are all new or rewritten code that has never run; the 1-step manual smoke mitigates but does not eliminate this, and an undetected bug consumes one of the two allowed training failures.

Budget optics: the 65 -> 78 amendment, though justified as a preexisting design flaw, is being made after attempt 1's negative result and pushes v2+v3 task totals to a possible 183 against v2's 170-task note; the restriction clause and unchanged GPU-hour cap are the defense, and this must be disclosed in the final report.
